added_lines: for our young parishioners october is the month of the holy rosary. it is also the month of the missions. the mission rosary helps children on every continent to pray for one another . follow the instructions to colour each decade of this rosary beads to create your own mission rosary. joyful mysteries monday, saturday sorrowful mysteries tuesday, friday luminous mysteries thursday glorious mysteries wednesday, sunday *the annunciation *the visitation *the nativity *the presentation *the finding in the temple *the agony in the garden *the scourging at the pillar *the crowning with thorns *the carrying of the cross *the crucifixion *the baptism of jesus *the wedding feast at cana *the proclamation of the kingdom *the transfiguration *the institution of the eucharist *the resurrection *the ascension *the descent of the holy spirit *the assumption *the coronation vol. 36 no. 32 11th october 2026 twenty eighth sunday in ordinary time this week’s readings first reading: isaiah 25:6-10a responsorial psalm: psalm 23 second reading: philippians 4:12-14, 19-20 gospel: matthew 22:1-14 or 22:1-10 key theme: god’s invitation to joy focus: faith and readiness summary: god welcomes everyone to his feast. he p rovides comfort, strength, and hope. we must accept his invitation with ready h earts. challenge: trust god in both plenty and need. res pond to his call with faith. live in a way that shows you are ready. action step: welcome someone who feels left out t his week. verse to remember: “invite to the feast whomever you find.” (matthew 2 2:9) sunday's scriptures the feast is ready god does not wait for us to be worthy before inviting us to his table. through isaiah, he promises a banquet for peoples, where death is destroyed and every tear wiped away. in the gospel, the king sends his serva nts to the crossroads: “invite everyone you can find.” the feast is ready— but we must come clothed in the grace he gives, not in our own self- sufficiency. st paul, even in prison, learned that christ is enough: “there is nothing i cannot master with the help of the one who gives me strength.” at mass, we taste that heavenly banquet. let us accept the invitation, put on christ, and bring others to the feast. come —everything is ready. world mission sunday – 18 october 2026 sunday, 18th october, the church marks 100 years o f world mission sunday, with the theme “missionaries of hope among all peoples.” it is the holy father’s official day of prayer and support for ove rseas missions, coordinated in ireland by mission ireland. how we can help: - pray for missionaries and young churches. - offer small sacrifices and acts of kindness. - give generously to the mission sunday collection/ envelopes. your support helps bring the gospel, education, hea lthcare and pastoral care to communities in need. please give what you can. thank you. mooncoin

next edition of the newsletter 18th october 2026 many thanks to all who contributed so generously to the hospice coffee morning held recently in comerfords. the success of this fundraiser reflects the efforts of those who helped so willingly on day. special thanks to marjorie for her jam sales o f €242 and to kathleen & cora for their cakes. the total amount collected was €1,792. rene. in november we remember. they are not gone from us, but gone before us. november is a time for remembering and praying for our loved ones who have gone before us and whose loss we feel. it is a time when we are partic ularly conscious of those in our parishes who are grieving and also all those families who have lost loved ones in the past year. we have a list of the deceased in the parish, and they will be prayed for at the masses, but we are kindly asking any parishioner who has experienced the loss of a loved one outside of the parish in the last year (november 2025 to november 2026) to contact the parish office

if they would like to have them remembered at any of the memorial masses (dates below). dates for november masses for deceased members of our parish community as fol lows: mooncoin: sat 7th nov. kilnaspic: sun 8th nov. carrigeen: sun 15th nov. this year, during the month of november, on the fol lowing sundays, you are invited to join fr martin in saying the rosary and for the blessing of graves in portnascully (8th november), rathkieran (15th novem ber) and ballytarsney (22th november). more details will follow so keep an eye on the news letter. christmas craft fair in the parish hall. we are holding our christmas craft fair on sunday 13th december from 11am - 4pm. we are inviting those interested in a table to email

with a brief description of your crafts. october the month of the holy rosary. october is dedicated to the holy rosary. praying the rosary at home, even a decade a day, draws families closer to jesus through mary and brings peace to the home. family prayer and sunday mass belong t ogether. the home is the “domestic church,” but we also need to gather each week as god’s family to hear his word and jesus in the eucharist. sunday mass is the heart of the week . let us make the rosary part of our homes and weekly mass the centre of our family life. our lady, pray for us. priests: fr. martin tobin adm.

please let us know who will be there on the night to present the candle candles will be supplied by the parish. major restoration of the church tower in recent times it has become apparent that there some significant structural problems in the tower of holy trinity church durrow. the wooden louvres (slanted beams) on all four sides of the tower are rotting, and each is framed in steel. these present a significant health and safety risk. when the tower was examined earlier in the summer other major difoculties with the pointing of stonework were also identified. the upshot of all this is that some major restoration work is necessary and as a matter of urgency. the work is scheduled to begin on monday next, 19th of october and will take approximately four to six weeks. the doors across the front of the church will remain locked during the work and entrance to the church will be through the side aisle doors only. the front of the church and the tower is a building site and therefore a health and safety risk. i realise this presents an inconvenience, but i ask for your consideration and cooperation. i am grateful to the parish finance committee and the diocesan authorities who have worked with me to address this problem. together with other necessary works to repair the lightning conductors on the church carried out earlier in the year, this major repair job will cost in the region of €90,000. your ongoing weekly financial support for the parish through the blue envelope collection was never more needed and appreciated. fr. martin best wishes to st brigid’s camogie
